sections.h2: Where is Pocatello, and what is it known for?
sections.html:
Pocatello is the home of Idaho State University, in the Portneuf Valley of southeastern Idaho. It has a Census Bureau population estimate of 58,771 for July 1, 2025, and about 33 square miles of land.

The city is named for Chief Pocatello, a 19th century Northern Shoshone leader. After its founding in 1889, Pocatello became known as the Gate City because pioneers on the Oregon Trail passed through the Portneuf Gap south of town, and the Union Pacific Railroad later made it a transportation junction. The Portneuf River runs along the western side of the city, and the city and the Portneuf Greenway Foundation have built more than 15 miles of trail along it since 1992.

For a seller, the railroad past and the river valley both matter. Older houses near the old rail corridor and homes close to the river each come with their own questions about condition, noise and drainage.

sections.h2: How did Pocatello grow into its current boundaries?
sections.html:
Pocatello absorbed the adjacent city of Alameda in 1962, and that merger made it the state's largest city by the 1960 census numbers. Chubbuck, to the north, opposed a similar merger and remains a separate city.

That detail has a practical side. A Chubbuck address follows that city's rules, not Pocatello's. Part of Pocatello also reaches into Power County, where the school district is American Falls Joint School District 381 rather than the Pocatello Chubbuck district. Confirm the jurisdiction for your parcel before you collect permit or tax information.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Pocatello housing?
sections.html:

sections.h2: Who are the biggest employers in Pocatello?
sections.html:
Education, health care and manufacturing lead the list. The city's 2023 Annual Financial Report names these top employers:

  • Idaho State University, with 2,500 to 4,999 employees.
  • Pocatello Chubbuck School District 25, Portneuf Medical Center and Idaho Central Credit Union, each with 1,000 to 2,499.
  • Amy's Kitchen, the City of Pocatello and ON Semiconductor, each with 500 to 999.
  • Bannock County with 430 employees, and Walmart with 250 to 499.

Idaho State University is a public university that became Idaho's second university in 1963. Its Holt Arena and performing arts center are local landmarks, and the campus sits above the lower Portneuf Valley.

sections.h2: What is Pocatello's climate, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Pocatello has a cold semi-arid continental climate, with hot summers and sharp winters. The all time high is 104 degrees Fahrenheit, reached several times including July 31, 2020, and the record low is minus 33 degrees on February 1, 1985.

The city building department lists a 3 foot frost level for foundation design, which is a useful clue to how deep the ground freezes. Frost heave can crack slabs, shift garage floors and open gaps at foundation edges.

  • Walk the foundation and look for diagonal cracks or doors that stick.
  • Check the garage slab and exterior concrete for lifting.
  • Look at roof condition after heavy snow years, and note the date of any repairs.

Foundation and roof questions are among the first things a buyer asks about. A cash buyer prices them without requiring you to repair them first.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and transit serve Pocatello?
sections.html:
The Bannock County portion of Pocatello belongs to the Pocatello Chubbuck School District 25, which runs three public high schools, four public middle schools and thirteen public elementary schools. Two public charter schools and several private schools add options.

Pocatello Regional Airport offers commercial air service. Pocatello Regional Transit runs buses on five hourly routes from Monday to Saturday, with no evening or Sunday service.

sections.h2: How do building permits work in Pocatello?
sections.html:
Pocatello's Building Department enforces codes for new construction and remodeling and handles the abatement of dangerous buildings. You apply for permits through the city's eTRAKiT online portal, and you can reach the department at 208-234-6158.

The city's code follows the International Building Code and the International Residential Code with local amendments, and permit fees are published each fiscal year. The fee schedule on the city site runs from October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2026.

  • Ask the Building Department whether past work on your house was permitted, since a buyer's inspector may ask.
  • If a dangerous building notice is on the property, tell us at the start, because it affects what a buyer can do.
  • Keep contractor receipts for the roof, furnace and water heater, which show the age of major systems.

See the Pocatello Building Department and the permit fee page.

sections.h2: How does Bannock County bill and collect property tax?
sections.html:
Bannock County mails tax bills by the fourth Monday in November, and the first half or the full year is due December 20. The second half is due June 20 of the following year, and both dates move to the next business day when they fall on a weekend.

Bannock County dateWhat happens
April 15Last day to apply for the Property Tax Reduction program
First Monday in JuneAssessment notices mailed
June 20Second half of the prior year due
Fourth Monday in JuneLast day to appeal to the Board of Equalization
Second Monday in JulyLast day of Board hearings
Fourth Monday in NovemberTreasurer mails bills
December 20First half or full payment due
December 31Last day to apply for the current year homeowner's exemption

Late interest on the second half is calculated at 1 percent per month back to January 1, so a payment only a few days late can carry about six months of interest. Bills for new construction and occupancy are on a separate roll, mailed in January and due in February. The Board of Equalization reviews whether the market value is fair and accurate, and it cannot lower a value because the tax is hard to pay.

The treasurer is in Room 203 of the Bannock County Courthouse at 624 E. Center St., and the phone number is 208-236-7260. See the Bannock County Property Tax Hub.

sections.h2: What should a Pocatello seller know before choosing a cash offer?
sections.html:
Idaho law requires sellers of one to four unit residential property to complete a property condition disclosure form under Idaho Code section 55-2501 and the sections after it. The form is where you describe known defects, and it applies whether you list the house or sell for cash. See Idaho Code 55-2508.

A cash sale suits owners facing a repair bill, an inherited house in another town, or a tenant problem. A listing may suit a house in good condition. We buy as-is, make an offer once we have the details, and you owe nothing if you say no. We do not promise a price before we see the property.

faqs.q: When are Bannock County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The full year or the first half is due December 20, and the second half is due June 20. If the 20th falls on a weekend, the due date moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Pocatello property assessment?
faqs.a: The deadline is the fourth Monday in June, and appeals go to the Bannock County Board of Equalization. Assessment notices are mailed the first Monday in June.

faqs.q: Is Pocatello in Bannock County only?
faqs.a: Most of it is, but part of the city extends into Power County. That part is served by American Falls Joint School District 381, so check your parcel before you gather tax and school information.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Pocatello house if it needs foundation or roof work?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to repair the foundation or the roof first. You still complete Idaho's seller disclosure form and describe the problems you know about.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Pocatello?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $271,000 for owner-occupied units in 2020 to 2024. That is a survey estimate for the whole city, so your own house may be worth more or less.
